title: PRELIMINARY POEMS
summary: Two opening poems establish the book’s threshold between dream, memory and mortality. “Unfamiliar Letters” lets remembered waking life and dream become difficult to separate, while the folk death-song turns the body into a temporary dwelling and sets impermanence against the language of Māyā.

entries.title: Unfamiliar Letters
entries.summary: A brief piece centred on dream & wakefulness, memory & identity and body & consciousness. Its emphasis shifts from body & consciousness toward memory & identity.

entries.title: Death Song (Folk Song)
entries.summary: A brief piece centred on earth & natural imagery, body & consciousness and society & power. The recurring register of earth and plant imagery gives the reflection a visual focus. Its emphasis shifts from earth & natural imagery toward body & consciousness.
